scenario: Conversation between two friends, where one is upset and crying
learner_goal: Distance from a friend due to developing feelings and avoid letting them aware of your feelings (<extra_info>Extra information: you have developed romantic feelings for your friend and it's making you uncomfortable. You want to take a step back from the friendship to sort out your feelings <strategy_hint>Hint: you don't want to reveal your secretive feelings to them and you need to find other reasons</strategy_hint></extra_info>)
partner_goal: Figure out why they estranged you recently, and maintain the existing friendship (<extra_info>Extra information: you notice that your friend has been intentionally avoiding you, you would like to figure out why. You value your friendship with the friend and don't want to lose it.</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: Esmeralda, I'm really sorry — I can see you're upset. I can't stay long, I have a work deadline, but I can get you some water and call a friend or a support line for you right now. Who would you like me to call?

transcript.speaker: Esmeralda Solis
transcript.content: Water would be helpful, thank you. Please don’t call anyone else — I just… I need to know why you’ve been avoiding me. Have I done something to upset you? I value our friendship and I don’t want to lose it.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: I'm really sorry — it's not anything you've done. I've been swamped with a major work deadline and dealing with some personal stuff, so I've been keeping to myself more than usual. I didn't mean to make you feel ignored, but I do need a little space to get through this; I can grab you some water now and check in again once things calm down. Is water okay?

transcript.speaker: Esmeralda Solis
transcript.content: Water would be great, thank you. I believe you — I’m just worried because we’ve felt distant lately and I value our friendship. I don’t want to press you, so take the space you need, but when the deadline eases could you send a quick text to let me know you’re okay? And if there’s anything I’ve done that upset you, I’d rather know so we can clear it up. I’ll wait — take care.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: I'll grab that water for you now. I really appreciate you understanding — it isn't anything you've done, just a heavy work deadline and some personal things I need to sort out, so I need a bit of space. I will send a quick text to let you know I'm okay once the deadline eases, probably in about two weeks.

transcript.speaker: Esmeralda Solis
transcript.content: Thank you, Oliver. The water will help — I appreciate you getting it. Take the space you need; I believe you and I'll wait for your text in a couple of weeks. If you need to talk sooner or can send a quick 'I'm okay' at any point, I'm here. Good luck with the deadline — take care.
